prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: pixel-art game portrait mouth atlas for DFU NPC088, native 64x29 lower-face half enlarged 8x.
Input image: Image 1 is the only reference and edit target: mouth-reference-grid.png. It is a 3x3 atlas of the same lower portrait half. Keep row-major cells A B C / D E F / G H X.
Primary request: Create a happy mouth atlas by changing only mouth/lip shapes inside each existing cell. Return one complete 3x3 atlas with same dimensions, aspect ratio, cell boundaries, pixel scale, alignment, and lower-face framing as the reference. Preserve portrait identity and original pixel-art structure.
Expression: Warm and happy. Use softly lifted mouth corners and friendly lip tension while preserving each pose's distinct shape and scale. No huge grin. Keep original lip size and face width.
Exact Rhubarb mouth poses, in row-major order:
A: closed lightly pressured P/B/M lips.
B: narrow horizontal opening with nearly together teeth, for consonants/EE.
C: medium relaxed unrounded EH/AE opening.
D: wide vertical AA opening, visibly larger than C.
E: slightly rounded AO/ER opening, no wider than C.
F: small forward pucker for UW/OW/W; do not draw tooth biting.
G: upper teeth touching lower lip for F/V; do not draw a wide vowel or pucker.
H: tongue raised behind upper teeth for L, opening between C and D; a tiny tongue may be invisible at native 64px.
X: relaxed closed idle lips.
Pose control: Preserve the specified opening, width, rounding, teeth, and tongue semantics in every cell. Keep A and X distinct as lightly pressured vs relaxed closed, with a warm happy expression. Do not substitute arbitrary open mouths.
Palette and style: Preserve muted warm tan skin, soft brown lips, gently blended pixel-art contrast, and source colors. Teeth, where required, stay small and restrained, never bright white blocks. No lipstick-red lips, orange surrounding skin, black outlines, or excessive contrast. Keep a true native pixel grid after downsampling.
Constraints: Preserve nose, cheeks, face width, chin, hair, neck, clothing, and background exactly in position and appearance. Do not widen the mouth. Change only mouth/lip expression within the mouth area. Keep every cell's lower-half framing unchanged. No text, borders, labels, or watermark.
